# Test files for `ink-media`

These MP3 files are made by `make-fixtures.sh` (it needs `ffmpeg` with
`libmp3lame`). Each is a **sine wave generated by the script, 0.5 seconds
long; none contains anyone else's work.** They are part of this repository
and are under the same license as the repository (GPL-3.0-or-later).

これらの MP3 は、`make-fixtures.sh` が生成した正弦波（0.5 秒）です。**他者の著作物を含みません。**
リポジトリと同じライセンス（GPL-3.0-or-later）で扱います。

| File | Format | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `tone-48k-stereo-gapless.mp3` | 48 kHz, stereo, with the Xing / LAME header (delay and padding) | Decodes to exactly the right length and starts at once (gapless playback) |
| `tone-44k-stereo-id3.mp3` | 44.1 kHz, stereo, with an ID3v2 tag in front | The tag is skipped and the audio is read |
| `tone-44k-mono.mp3` | 44.1 kHz, mono | Mono is copied to both channels |
| `tone-48k-stereo-no-header.mp3` | 48 kHz, stereo, **without** the Xing / LAME header | Starts with a short silence: the known limit of MP3 loops (ADR-0009) |

The left channel is a 440 Hz cosine wave and the right channel is 660 Hz
(the mono file has 440 Hz only), with an amplitude of 0.5. A cosine starts
at its peak, so a silence at the start of a decoded file can be told apart
from the sound.

WAV files are not kept here: the tests make them in memory (`src/test_util.rs`).

## Making the files again

```bash
./make-fixtures.sh
```

The script uses the `bitexact` flags, so the same `ffmpeg` / LAME gives the
same files. A different version may give files that differ in a few bytes;
the tests check lengths, frequencies and levels, not the bytes.
